analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the story of the morning flipped from a mechanical dip-buying bounce to a genuine catalyst — Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president at ~8:55 AM ET, 11 days after his resignation, after receiving input from senior US government levels and concluding the reinstatement poses no national security risk. NVDA went from +9% premarket to +30% (Reuters: +33% in early trading), and the Nasdaq's gain roughly doubled from the premarket print (+3% futures to +5.7-6.7% cash). The open still leaves the S&P about 9% below its October record, so this is a recovery of Friday's damage, not a new high. What did NOT change: the independent investigation into reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort continues, Colette Kress stays CFO after her interim-CEO stint, Bessent's Nov 25 shell-company deadline and the SEC accounting probe remain open, and Capital Economics still calls the move a likely 'dead cat bounce' while BCA warns the market 'failed to find a floor.' Anthropic is the tell on fading euphoria: +4% premarket, then down 1.3% by 9:54 AM ET after opening at $93.65. The CrowdStrike-Zscaler deal is the second confirmed M&A signal that dealmaking continues through the drawdown, with the market again charging the buyer. Signal vs noise: the Huang reinstatement (confirmed by the company, 8-K filed) and the breadth of the AI rebound are signal; the size of the first-30-minutes pop is noise until the close in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape. No qualifying HN or Reddit thread surfaced.

headlines.headline: Stocks surged at the open: S&P 500 +4.06% at 7,190.70, Nasdaq +5.72% at 23,910.56, Dow +2.44% at 49,321.80 as of 9:48 AM ET (Pulsafi); CNN had the Nasdaq +6.7% and S&P +4.7% right after the 9:30 AM ET bell. SPY +3.4% at 9:31 AM ET per regardsofwallstreet.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket bounce held and strengthened into the cash open, recovering most of Friday's 3.7% S&P drop — but the S&P is still roughly 9% below its October record, so this is damage repair, not a new high.

headlines.headline: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately, by unanimous board vote announced ~8:55 AM ET; the board said it received input from senior US government levels and is confident the reinstatement poses no national security risk. NVDA +30% (CNN) / +33% in early trading (Reuters) after losing a third of its value in two weeks. The independent investigation into reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort continues; interim CEO Colette Kress remains CFO. Trump praised the decision on Truth Social.
headlines.why_it_matters: Removes the single biggest overhang on the AI trade — the leadership vacuum and national-security cloud at the sector's bellwether — which is why the whole Nasdaq roughly doubled its premarket gain on the news.

headlines.headline: CrowdStrike's $43.9B all-stock acquisition of Zscaler (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share) is live in the market: CRWD -9.66% to $207.27 and ZS +17.02% to $227.98 as of 9:54 AM ET (Finnhub).
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest cybersecurity deal ever is confirmed and trading — the market is again charging the buyer and paying the target, the same pattern as the premarket read, and M&A is still moving through the drawdown.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) faded after the open: last $87.73 at 9:54 AM ET, -1.33% vs Friday's $88.91 close, after opening at $93.65 and touching $94.24 (Finnhub). It had been +4.1% premarket to $92.59.
headlines.why_it_matters: The newest mega-IPO gave back its whole premarket gain within 25 minutes of the open — a small warning that the relief rally is not lifting everything, and IPO euphoria is still fragile.

headlines.headline: AI breadth is strong at the open: CoreWeave +18.45% to $46.80 (Finnhub, 9:53 AM ET; CNN had +27% shortly after the bell), Dell +7.9% and Sandisk +7.4% premarket (Barron's). Megacaps were broadly higher premarket: Alphabet +5.1%, Tesla +4.22% to $360.40, Meta +3.25% to $579.07, Amazon +3.1%, Microsoft +2.70% to $497.58, Apple +1.01% to $346.03 (IBD/Finnhub, ~8:53 AM ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is broad across AI hardware, neocloud and megacaps, not just Nvidia — but Anthropic's fade shows buyers are still selective within the rally.

headlines.headline: Counterweight: Capital Economics called Monday's move a 'dead cat bounce' — 'just such a big sell-off... and got a bit overdone' — and warned 'another substantial selloff is quite likely' given the S&P is down more than 10% from its Oct 6 high so quickly (CNN). BCA Research this morning warned the market 'failed to find a floor.' VIX is down to 26.80 but still far above its pre-rout level; 10Y yield rose 6bp intraday to 4.97%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two named houses are explicitly fading the bounce — if the open's gains are mostly mechanical short-covering into a thin holiday week, the close is the real test.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news today. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 results (Nov 3) — revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.1M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit vs $0.26 a year ago, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M and DCF to $495-505M; J-W Power integration completed into SAP on Oct 1, leverage 3.78x vs 3.75x target; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6.

watch_next: S&P Global November flash PMI, released 9:45 AM ET — the first data read of the holiday-shortened week; the print was not yet in sourced coverage at brief time.
Whether the open's gains hold into the 4:00 PM ET close — Capital Economics and BCA are both fading the bounce, and VIX futures were up ~10% even as spot VIX fell.
Earnings after the close today: HPE, Agilent, Zoom — HPE is the first check on the reported supplier price hikes (FT: Dell, HPE, Supermicro hiking prices up to 45%).
Wednesday's data dump before Thanksgiving: core PCE (expected ~3.2% y/y), Q3 GDP, durable goods, jobless claims, Beige Book — the next real test for the near-certain December Fed hike.
Nvidia's ongoing independent investigation, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline on shell companies, and the SEC accounting probe — none resolved by the reinstatement.
